easy.q: How many U.S. states meet at the Four Corners Monument?
easy.fact: It's the only spot where four states touch: Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah.

easy.q: How many Cars movies has Pixar released?
easy.fact: The first one, in 2006, made Lightning McQueen a star.

easy.q: What number does the Roman numeral C stand for?
easy.fact: C comes from centum, Latin for one hundred.

easy.q: How many bases are on a baseball diamond, counting home plate?
easy.fact: Home plate is the only base that isn't a square bag.

easy.q: How many musketeers are in the title of Alexandre Dumas's famous novel?
easy.fact: The hero, d'Artagnan, makes it four by the end.

medium.q: How many pounds does the shot weigh in men's Olympic shot put?
medium.fact: The women's shot weighs about 8.8 pounds.

medium.q: Interstate 95 runs from Florida to Maine. How many states does it pass through?
medium.fact: It also runs through Washington, D.C.

medium.q: The U.S. started building the Panama Canal in 1904. How many years later did it open?
medium.fact: It opened on Aug. 15, 1914, just as World War I began.

medium.q: In what year did Grey's Anatomy premiere?
medium.fact: It's the longest-running scripted prime-time show in ABC history.

medium.q: How many official James Bond movies did Sean Connery star in, not counting 1983's Never Say Never Again?
medium.fact: His first was Dr. No in 1962.

hard.q: In what year was the Rosetta Stone found in Egypt?
hard.fact: French soldiers dug it up while rebuilding a fort near the town of Rashid.

hard.q: What's the hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth, in Death Valley, in °F?
hard.fact: It was recorded at Furnace Creek on July 10, 1913.

hard.q: In 2015, Klay Thompson set the NBA record for points in one quarter. How many did he score?
hard.fact: He made all 13 of his shots in that third quarter, including nine 3-pointers.

hard.q: How many letters are in supercalifragilisticexpialidocious, from Mary Poppins?
hard.fact: Mary Poppins won five Oscars, including Best Actress for Julie Andrews.
